name: create-chat
description:
Create a new chat object.

💡 TIP: Creates a new 1:1 or group Teams chat. Body: { chatType ('oneOnOne' or 'group'), topic (optional, group only), members: [{ '@odata.type': '#microsoft.graph.aadUserConversationMember', roles: ['owner' | 'guest'], 'user@odata.bind': 'https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/users({id})' }] }. A oneOnOne chat requires exactly 2 members (self + other), both with role 'owner'. For group chats, include all participants. The signed-in user must be one of the members. Returns the created chat with its id — use that id with send-chat-message, list-chat-members, etc.

originalCreatedDateTime.description: Timestamp of the original creation time for the chat. The value is null if the chat never entered migration mode.

topic.description: (Optional) Subject or topic for the chat. Only available for group chats.

installedApps.description: A collection of all the apps in the chat. Nullable.

members.description: A collection of all the members in the chat. Nullable.

messages.description: A collection of all the messages in the chat. Nullable.

permissionGrants.description: A collection of permissions granted to apps for the chat.

pinnedMessages.description: A collection of all the pinned messages in the chat. Nullable.

tabs.description: A collection of all the tabs in the chat. Nullable.

targetedMessages.description: A collection of targeted messages in the chat that are visible only to specific users. Nullable. You can't expand this relationship using $expand. Targeted messages can also be retrieved via the userTeamwork: getAllTargetedMessages API.

name: send-chat-message
description:
Send a new chatMessage in the specified chat. This API can't create a new chat; you must use the list chats method to retrieve the ID of an existing chat before you can create a chat message.

💡 TIP: To @mention someone, put <at user-id="<aad-user-id>">Display Name</at> in the html content; the server numbers the tag and builds the mentions array. Use the userId field (not id) from list-team-members or list-chat-members. Use contentType 'html' in the body — plain text contentType gets mangled by Graph API. Alternatively, hand-build the raw form: put an <at id="0">Name</at> tag in the html content and add a mentions array to the request body, as a sibling of the body property (not a separate top-level tool parameter): { body: { contentType: 'html', content: 'Hi <at id="0">Name</at>' }, mentions: [{ id: 0, mentionText: 'Name', mentioned: { user: { id: '<aad-user-id>', displayName: 'Name', userIdentityType: 'aadUser' } } }] }. Each mention id must match its <at id> value; include userIdentityType: 'aadUser' or Graph returns 400 'value without a type name'.

description:

To find Teams meetings, use $select=subject,start,isOnlineMeeting,onlineMeetingProvider,onlineMeeting and keep events with isOnlineMeeting true and onlineMeetingProvider teamsForBusiness. Teams meetings expose their join link as onlineMeeting/joinUrl; match it against the normalized joinWebUrl from parse-teams-url.

name: create-calendar-event
description:
Create (schedule) a new calendar event — a meeting or appointment — on the user's calendar. Times use nested objects, not flat fields: start: {dateTime, timeZone}, end: {dateTime, timeZone}. Do NOT use startDateTime/startTimeZone. For one-off events, UTC is simplest (e.g. 3:30 PM AEDT = 04:30 UTC). For recurring events, use the organizer's own time zone name instead — Graph resolves DST against the zone in start.timeZone, so UTC drifts after DST changes. Get the zone from get-calendar-view, or validate one with IANA or Windows time zone names instead of guessing from memory. Set subject, location, body, and attendees; supports online meetings and recurrence.

💡 TIP: CRITICAL: Do not try to guess the email address of the recipients. Use the list-outlook-contacts tool to find the email address of the recipients.

name: reply-to-channel-message
description:
Create a new reply to a chatMessage in a specified channel.

💡 TIP: To @mention someone, put <at user-id="<aad-user-id>">Display Name</at> in the html content; the server numbers the tag and builds the mentions array. Use the userId field (not id) from list-team-members or list-chat-members. Use contentType 'html' in the body — plain text contentType gets mangled by Graph API. Alternatively, hand-build the raw form: put an <at id="0">Name</at> tag in the html content and add a mentions array to the request body, as a sibling of the body property (not a separate top-level tool parameter): { body: { contentType: 'html', content: 'Hi <at id="0">Name</at>' }, mentions: [{ id: 0, mentionText: 'Name', mentioned: { user: { id: '<aad-user-id>', displayName: 'Name', userIdentityType: 'aadUser' } } }] }. Each mention id must match its <at id> value; include userIdentityType: 'aadUser' or Graph returns 400 'value without a type name'.

attachments.description: References to attached objects like files, tabs, meetings etc.

chatId.description: If the message was sent in a chat, represents the identity of the chat.

createdDateTime.description: Timestamp of when the chat message was created.

importance.description: The importance of the chat message: normal, high, or urgent.

locale.description: Locale of the chat message set by the client. Always set to en-us.

mentions.description: List of entities mentioned in the chat message. Supported entities are: user, bot, team, channel, chat, and tag.

messageHistory.description: List of activity history of a message item, including modification time and actions, such as reactionAdded, reactionRemoved, or reaction changes, on the message.

messageType.description: The type of chat message. Default is message.

reactions.description: Reactions for this chat message (for example, Like).

subject.description: The subject of the chat message, in plaintext.

summary.description: Summary text of the chat message that could be used for push notifications and summary views or fall back views. Only applies to channel chat messages, not chat messages in a chat.

hostedContents.description: Content in a message hosted by Microsoft Teams - for example, images or code snippets.

replies.description: Replies for a specified message. Supports $expand for channel messages.

teamId.description: Value for the 'teamId' path segment. Pass it under the name 'teamId', not as 'id'. Use the 'id' field of the team object as returned by Microsoft Graph.

channelId.description: Value for the 'channelId' path segment. Pass it under the name 'channelId', not as 'id'. Use the 'id' field of the channel object as returned by Microsoft Graph.

chatMessageId.description: Value for the 'chatMessageId' path segment. Pass it under the name 'chatMessageId', not as 'id'. Use the 'id' field of the chat message object as returned by Microsoft Graph.

includeHeaders.description: Include response headers (including ETag) in the response metadata

excludeResponse.description: Exclude the full response body and only return success or failure indication

name: list-team-members
description:
Get the conversationMember collection of a team. The membership IDs returned by the server must be treated as opaque strings. The client shouldn't try to parse or make assumptions about these resource IDs. In the future, membership results can include users from various tenants, as indicated in the response. Clients should avoid assuming that all members exclusively belong to the current tenant.

💡 TIP: Lists members of a team. Each member has displayName, email, roles and userId. Pass name to keep only members whose displayName or email contains that text (case-insensitive); use the returned userId in an @mention.

top.description: Maximum number of items to return per page (Graph $top).

teamId.description: Value for the 'teamId' path segment. Pass it under the name 'teamId', not as 'id'. Use the 'id' field of the team object as returned by Microsoft Graph.

fetchAllPages.description: Follow @odata.nextLink across pages (up to 100 pages, 5,000 items, or 20 MiB total) and merge results into one response.

name.description: Case-insensitive substring filter matched client-side against each member's displayName and email.

includeHeaders.description: Include response headers (including ETag) in the response metadata

excludeResponse.description: Exclude the full response body and only return success or failure indication

name: parse-teams-url
description: Converts any Teams meeting URL format (short /meet/, full /meetup-join/, or recap ?threadId=) into a standard joinWebUrl and extracts meeting identifiers. Match the returned joinWebUrl against onlineMeeting/joinUrl in get-calendar-view results, or use threadId with get-chat / list-chat-messages.

url.description: Teams meeting URL in any format

name: read-mail-text
description: Read email messages as clean plain text with unwrapped tracking/SafeLinks URLs, stripped reply quotes, and expanded attachment metadata (id, name, contentType, size, isInline). Provide either messageIds (up to 20 message IDs) or folderId (e.g. 'inbox'). Each message body is truncated at maxChars runes (default 3000) within a 300,000-rune aggregate budget across the call (marking truncated: true and fullLength).

messageIds.description: Ids of the messages to read (max 20). Give messageIds or folderId, not both.

folderId.description: Folder to read from: a well-known name (inbox, sentitems, drafts, archive, deleteditems, junkemail) or a folder id.

top.description: With folderId: how many messages, newest first (default and max 20).

filter.description: With folderId: OData $filter, e.g. receivedDateTime ge 2026-10-01T00:00:00Z or from/emailAddress/address eq 'a@example.com'.

search.description: With folderId: KQL search, e.g. from:paul subject:"quarterly report" (quoting is normalised as for list-mail-messages). Graph cannot combine it with filter.

maxChars.description: Maximum characters (UTF-8 runes) of body text to return per message (default 3000, subject to a 300,000-rune aggregate budget across the call).

name: get-download-url
description: Mint a short-lived, single-use host-side download URL (/attachment?t=...) for Microsoft Graph binary content (such as /drives/{drive-id}/items/{driveItem-id}/content or /me/messages/{message-id}/attachments/{attachment-id}/$value). Pass the returned downloadUrl to download_url to save the file into your workspace. Returns { downloadUrl, expiresAt, singleUse, name?, size?, contentType? }.

target.description: Relative Microsoft Graph path starting with "/", such as /drives/{drive-id}/items/{driveItem-id}/content, /me/drive/items/{driveItem-id}/content, /sites/{site-id}/drive/items/{driveItem-id}, or /me/messages/{message-id}/attachments/{attachment-id}/$value. A trailing /content is optional for drive items.
